2608.20116.title: When Text and Numbers Disagree: Evidence Arbitration in Large Language Models
2608.20116.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in settings where textual summaries, numerical observations, and external tool outputs may provide conflicting evidence. We study how LLMs arbitrate between such sources when they support opposing decisions. To do so, we introduce a controlled synthetic benchmark in which latent risk trajectories generate both numerical time series and natural language summaries, allowing us to construct conflicts where exactly one evidence source is aligned with the ground-truth label. This design lets us independently manipulate modality, temporal recency, source reliability, and evidence provenance. Across open-weight instruction-tuned models, we find that arbitration behaviour is systematic rather than random: models exhibit distinct text-versus-number preferences, follow temporal recency more consistently than explicit reliability cues, and can over-rely on external forecasts even when they conflict with direct contextual evidence. These results suggest that current LLMs often rely on heuristic arbitration strategies when integrating heterogeneous evidence, highlighting a failure mode for tool-augmented decision systems.
2608.20116.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在文本摘要、數值觀察和外部工具輸出可能提供相互矛盾的證據的情境中越來越多地被使用。<lb/>我們研究LLMs如何在支持相對立決策的這些來源之間進行仲裁。<lb/>為此，我們引入了一個受控的合成基準，其中潛在的風險軌跡生成數值時間序列和自然語言摘要，讓我們能夠構建衝突，其中恰好有一個證據來源與真實標籤一致。<lb/>這種設計使我們能夠獨立操控模態、時間接近性、來源可靠性和證據來源。<lb/>在開放權重的指令調整模型中，我們發現仲裁行為是系統性的，而非隨機的：模型表現出明顯的文本與數字偏好，對時間接近性的遵循比對明確的可靠性提示更一致，並且即使在與直接上下文證據相矛盾時，也可能過度依賴外部預測。<lb/>這些結果表明，當整合異質證據時，當前的LLMs經常依賴啟發式的仲裁策略，突顯了工具增強決策系統的一種失效模式。
